name: National Space Traffic Management Policy
effect: Seeks to reduce the growing threat of orbital debris to the common interest of all nations; articulates the policy of the United States to pursue and utilize both Government and commercial sector technologies to track and monitor space debris; requires updates to the U.S. Orbital Debris Mitigation Standard Practices and new guidelines for satellite design and operation; sets guidelines for the United States to manage space traffic more effectively by spearheading new data sharing initiatives; recommends the provision of basic space situational awareness data and basic space traffic management services free of direct user fees; directs the DOC to make space safety data and services available to the public, while the DOD maintains the authoritative catalogue of space objects.
alignment_notes: Aligns with pillar 1 because it recommends providing basic space situational awareness data and basic space traffic management services. It also would implement free data sharing to the public. Also aligns with pillar 2 because it would track and monitor space debris. Does not address pillar 3.
sponsors: Scott Pace (Deputy Assistant to the President & Executive Secretary of the National Space Council)
